summary: The High Places: four high states crowned with standing stones older than any Sunhot record, quarrying the white stone that builds half the realms.

keepers_court.name: The Keepers' Court
keepers_court.desc: The keepers of the high places govern from a hall of white stone on the first ridge. They are shepherds, masons and pilgrims by turns, and they speak softly.

long_keeping.name: The Long Keeping
long_keeping.desc: The keepers have kept the high places longer than any record can say, and they intend to keep them longer still. Their patience is a kind of wealth.

songs_of_stones.name: Songs of the Old Stones
songs_of_stones.desc: Pilgrims who climb to the stones come down with songs in an old measure, and the shepherds teach them to their children. Nobody knows who made the songs, and nobody has stopped singing them.

masons.name: Masons of Godland
masons.desc: Godland's masons cut white stone so true that a wall of it needs no binding. Half the towns of the Lands of the Sun were raised by their hands.

the_old_stones.title: The Old Stones
the_old_stones.desc: At midsummer the pilgrims climb to the stones, as they have done for longer than anyone can say. Nobody remembers who raised them, and the keepers do not pretend to know.

options.name: Let them stand as they are
Read the marks on the stones

focuses.name: The High Places
focuses.desc: Godland is four high states named on the oldest maps, crowned with standing stones older than any Sunhot record. Its white stone builds half the towns of the south.

focuses.name: The Keeper of the High Places
focuses.desc: Aldoreth keeps the high places for the realm, as a long line of keepers has done before. He is the oldest in the court and the quietest.

focuses.name: The Keepers' Law
focuses.desc: The law of the keepers is short, written on a single stone and read aloud each midsummer. Every shepherd and mason knows it, and few have broken it.

focuses.name: The Four Lands
focuses.desc: Paths of laid stone join the four states, with cairns at each bend and a well at every fork. Walkers say the roads are easier to follow than to leave.

focuses.name: The Keepers' Council
focuses.desc: The keepers of the four states meet on the first ridge each equinox. They bring pebbles from their own hills, and set them in a ring on the council table.

focuses.name: The Long Keeping
focuses.desc: The keepers write down every season's events in a book of thin stone leaves. The book is older than the hall, and is kept in a niche of its own.

focuses.name: The Old Stones
focuses.desc: Standing stones crown the high places, grey and weathered and marked with signs nobody reads. Pilgrims climb to them at midsummer, and the keepers do not say what the stones are.

focuses.name: The Stone-Readers
focuses.desc: Scholars take rubbings of the marks and compare them in the keepers' hall. They agree on very little, and have filled a hundred sheets with their disagreement.

focuses.name: The Sanctuary Paths
focuses.desc: Paths of dressed stone lead to the high places, with rest-huts and water at every league. The keepers ask that pilgrims walk and not ride.

focuses.name: Pilgrims to the High Places
focuses.desc: Pilgrims arrive in long lines, from valleys that have never heard of Godland and from towns that have. They bring no gifts, and the keepers ask for none.

focuses.name: The Hidden Terraces
focuses.desc: Terraces cut into the north faces of the mountains catch the last light of the day. They grow barley, beans and a small yellow apple.

focuses.name: Songs of the Old Stones
focuses.desc: The songs that pilgrims bring down from the stones are gathered and sung in the keepers' hall. Their measure is older than the hall, and nobody has changed a word of them.

focuses.name: Carry the Stones' Tale to Gala
focuses.desc: Some tales are too old for anyone in Godland to explain, and the keepers have chosen to send them to Gala. A messenger goes south with a packet of rubbings and a sealed letter.

effects.tooltip: A tale too old for anyone here to explain.

focuses.name: White Stone Quarries
focuses.desc: Godland's white stone is cut from the lower slopes in great blocks, and the quarries are never worked at midsummer. Carters take the stone down in oxen-drawn sleds.

focuses.name: Masons of Godland
focuses.desc: The masons cut, square and dress the white stone, and their lodge is the oldest in the south. A mason's mark is as good as a seal.

focuses.name: The Stone Roads
focuses.desc: White stone roads descend from the quarries to the valley towns, each slab laid by a mason and checked by his master. They wear very slowly.

focuses.name: Walls of the High Places
focuses.desc: Walls of white stone are raised across the passes, plain and thick and as old-looking as the hills. If the danger comes, they will be ready.
